summary:
Centre Alliance is a South Australian centrist and socially liberal party founded in 2013 as the Nick Xenophon Team. It gained national attention in the 2016 federal election, electing three senators and MP Rebekha Sharkie, who won the seat of Mayo.

The party has since lost most of its parliamentary representation. Its Senate vote fell sharply in 2019, and no new senators were elected. In 2022, Sharkie was its only candidate and retained Mayo. By 2025, she was the party’s sole member, remaining in Centre Alliance partly because of money held in its accounts.

The party changed its name to Centre Alliance in 2018 after withdrawing a bid to become SA-BEST (Federal). Its positions combine social liberalism and populism, including support for climate action, same-sex marriage, veterans, Australian manufacturing and euthanasia.
